title: Audit logging: add residency.policy_evaluated + residency.violation events (SIEM field mapping)
author: Nadia Rahman
release_notes: Adds two new audit event types for hosted data residency enforcement: residency.policy_evaluated (allow decisions) and residency.violation (deny decisions). Events include required tenant/actor/context fields and a stable SIEM-friendly mapping (Splunk/Sentinel). No behavior changes to request routing/enforcement in this PR; it only emits audit evidence for decisions already made by gateway enforcement middleware.
description: Context: Hosted data residency enforcement needs compliance-grade evidence for (a) every residency policy decision, and (b) violations that were denied. This PR adds two new audit log event types and wires emission into the gateway residency enforcement path. It also includes a canonical field mapping for downstream exporters (Splunk/Sentinel) so customers and GRC can build stable detections/controls. Linked: ENG-2844 (audit log events for residency decisions), PM-482 (initiative). Event types: 1) residency.policy_evaluated (emitted on allow). 2) residency.violation (emitted on deny / admission failure). Design notes: - Emission happens after policy evaluation but before model execution (same request span); events are emitted regardless of whether downstream tracing is enabled. - We intentionally emit allow events only when region pinning is enabled for the org/project to avoid high-volume noise for non-enterprise tenants. (This matches guidance from Olga/Marcus.) - Violation events are always emitted when enforcement denies a request (even if pinning was configured via inherited org defaults) since those are the compliance-relevant cases. Payload shape (selected fields): - event.type: "residency.policy_evaluated" | "residency.violation" - event.version: "1" - actor.type: "user" | "api_key" | "service" - actor.id: stable internal id when available - actor.email: populated for console-initiated changes/requests when present in auth context - tenant.org_id, tenant.project_id - request.id: internal request id - request.route: e.g. "/v1/chat/completions" - request.sdk: parsed from user-agent when present (e.g. redwood-sdk-python/1.18.0) - residency.pinned_region, residency.allowed_regions - residency.requested_region: parsed from endpoint region / client hint if provided - residency.effective_region: region selected by router/gateway - residency.decision: "allow" | "deny" - residency.reason_code: e.g. "REGION_MISMATCH", "FALLBACK_DISALLOWED", "POLICY_NOT_FOUND" - http.status_code: e.g. 403 - error.code: e.g. "RESIDENCY_REGION_MISMATCH" (when deny) SIEM export mapping: The audit envelope stays consistent with existing audit event formatting; this PR adds a mapping table (docs for internal exporter consumers) aligning to common schemas: - Splunk: sourcetype=redwood:audit, fields flattened with dot notation preserved - Sentinel (ASIM-ish): event_type -> EventType, actor.id -> ActorId, tenant.org_id -> TenantId, request.id -> CorrelationId, residency.* -> CustomDetails.* Testing: - Unit tests validate event schema + required fields presence. - Integration test verifies that a pinned EU org hitting a US endpoint emits residency.violation with reason_code=REGION_MISMATCH and includes request.id. Checklist: [x] Schema reviewed by Security Eng (Marcus) [x] Evidence fields reviewed by GRC (Olga) [x] Export mapping reviewed by SIEM owner (Kevin) [x] No PII beyond existing actor email behavior (email is already present in other audit events when user-authenticated; API-key traffic does not include email) [x] Added docs/comments for versioning strategy (event.version=1).
commits: audit: define residency audit event types + schema validators
gateway: emit residency.policy_evaluated on allow when pinning enabled
gateway: emit residency.violation on deny with reason_code + error.code
audit: add SIEM field mapping table + exporter notes
tests: add unit + integration coverage for residency audit events
conversation: Marcus Lin (review): Are we sure we want to emit allow events for every request? That could be extremely high volume for large tenants. Nadia Rahman (author): Agree. I scoped allow emission behind `residency_enforcement_enabled && policy.has_region_pinning` so we only emit for customers who actually turned on pinning (enterprise feature). Violations are always emitted because those are the audit-critical cases. Olga Petrov (review): Need explicit fields for tenant/org/project, the policy inputs (pinned/allowed), and the decision reason. Also please confirm event versioning. Nadia Rahman (author): Added tenant.org_id + tenant.project_id. Included residency.pinned_region + residency.allowed_regions + residency.reason_code. Added event.version=1 and a short versioning note in packages/audit/src/versioning.md. Kevin Osei (review): For Splunk/Sentinel, we need stable flattened fields. Can you add a mapping table and ensure request.id is included for correlation? Nadia Rahman (author): Added packages/audit/src/flattening/siem_field_mapping.md with canonical field names and examples; request.id is now required in the schema and included in both event types. Allison Grant (review): Make sure we don’t log full URL or query params; route is fine. Also add consistent naming with other audit events (event.type, actor.*, tenant.*). Nadia Rahman (author): Confirmed we only log request.route (no query string) and followed the same audit envelope naming conventions. Ethan Park (review): Please ensure we don’t emit allow events if policy evaluator is unreachable and we fail open (if that ever happens). Nadia Rahman (author): In the current gateway enforcement, residency evaluation failures fail closed when pinning enabled; but I guarded allow emission to only happen after a successful evaluation path. Added a test for error path that ensures no allow event is emitted. Marcus Lin (final): Approved. Olga Petrov (final): Approved, meets evidence needs. Kevin Osei (final): Approved; exporter mapping is sufficient for beta.
